scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) and pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) report they cannot
reach each other, though each can still ping its own gateway (10.0.0.1
and 10.0.1.1). The odd part, per the NOC: every BGP session in the
fabric is Established and no interface has flapped -- but the spines'
routing tables no longer contain the 10.0.0.0/24 prefix at all, while
10.0.1.0/24 is still there. Investigate.

injection.action: remove the host-subnet network advertisement from BGP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_0 BGP network advertisement
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_0 (AS 65200) is supposed to advertise its host
  subnet with `network 10.0.0.0/24` under `router bgp 65200`. That
  statement was removed, so bgpd immediately withdrew the prefix; the
  spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 all lose their route to
  10.0.0.0/24 while every session stays Established. Traffic from
  pc_0_0 toward pc_0_1 is still delivered (leaf_router_0_0 still learns
  10.0.1.0/24), but the return traffic has no route back to
  10.0.0.0/24 and dies in the fabric -- so the ping fails in both
  directions.
Localization: leaf_router_0_0
Root cause: `network 10.0.0.0/24` missing from `router bgp 65200` on
  leaf_router_0_0
Fix: re-add the network statement on leaf_router_0_0 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
Re-add the advertisement on leaf_router_0_0:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 65200"
 -c "network 10.0.0.0/24"`
Note: the injection changed only the running config; the intended
config is still intact in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so `service frr restart`
on leaf_router_0_0 is an equally correct fix.
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: missing BGP network advertisement for 10.0.0.0/24
must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: all BGP sessions Established and links UP while exactly one prefix (10.0.0.0/24) is absent from the fabric tables
bonus-explains-return-path: explains that packets toward pc_0_1 are still delivered but replies have no route back to 10.0.0.0/24 (or equivalently that only the withdrawn direction is unroutable)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault lies in leaf_router_0_0's BGP configuration: the router is
missing the `network 10.0.0.0/24` origination statement inside an
`address-family ipv4 unicast` block. As a result, although 10.0.0.0/24
is correctly present as a directly connected route in the kernel FIB, it
is never injected into the BGP RIB and therefore never advertised to the
upstream spines (spine_router_0_0 via 172.16.0.4 / AS 65100, and
spine_router_0_1 via 172.16.0.8 / AS 65101). Both BGP sessions on
leaf_router_0_0 are fully Established and the router does send one
prefix — but that prefix is 10.0.1.0/24, which it learned from the
fabric and re-advertises; it originates nothing of its own. The spines
and super_spine therefore have no reachable path to 10.0.0.0/24, and
leaf_router_0_1 (gateway for pc_0_1) equally has no return route,
making the pc_0_0 ↔ pc_0_1 path black-holed in both directions. The
peer router leaf_router_0_1 has the correct configuration (`address-family
ipv4 unicast` / `network 10.0.1.0/24`), confirming this is a
per-device misconfiguration rather than a fabric-wide policy issue.

Root cause: The `network 10.0.0.0/24` statement was never added to
leaf_router_0_0's BGP address-family, so the connected prefix is never
originated into the BGP fabric.

Corrective fix: On leaf_router_0_0, enter vtysh and add:
  router bgp 65200
   address-family ipv4 unicast
    network 10.0.0.0/24
   exit-address-family
This will cause leaf_router_0_0 to originate 10.0.0.0/24 into BGP,
propagating it to both spines and the super-spine, restoring full
pc_0_0 ↔ pc_0_1 reachability.
